newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-AAMODT ON COURSE FOR COMBINED GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AAMODT ON COURSE FOR COMBINED GOLD.

text.p: Kjetil Andre Aamodt moved into position to claim Norway's second gold medal at the Alpine skiing world championships by posting the second fastest time in the downhill leg of the men's combined on Thursday.

While Austrian downhill specialist Werner Franz clocked the fastest time down the Kandahar Banchetta course with one minute 37.20 seconds, Olympic and world silver medallist Aamodt was close behind in 1:37.37.
Aamodt, the 1993 world championship slalom champion, was expected to do better than Franz in the two slalom legs of the combined later on Thursday (first run 1700 GMT, second run 2000 GMT).

This season, Aamodt has made one appearance on the World Cup slalom podium with a third place in Park City and he was fourth in both Breckenridge and Wengen. He was also second in both World Cup combined events last month.

His compatriot and reigning Olympic combined champion Lasse Kjus posted the third best downhill time -- equal with Swiss downhiller Bruno Kernen on 1:37.62 -- and the pair could make it Norway's second one-two at these championships.
At last Monday's world championship super-G, Kjus took silver behind compatriot Atle Skaardal.
Although Kjus won the World Cup combined in Kitzbuehel, his performance in slalom has been poor this winter. He has completed only two slaloms and was 20th on both occasions.
Austria's biggest hope for this event, Guenther Mader, who has four world championship combined bronze medals, disappointed with only the 14th best downhill time of 1:38.64.
Mader, winner of the World Cup combination in Chamonix, was still optimistic and said: "The time difference is not that big, I still have a chance to make the podium."
His compatriot Christian Mayer was lying eighth in 1:38.48 and was also in the running for a podium position. Mayer's best slalom showing this winter was a fourth place in Park City.
